newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Red Cross pension fund assets grow 12 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross pension fund assets grow 12 pct in 1996.

text.p: Assets managed by the pension fund of the Swiss-run International Committee of the Red Cross grew 12 percent in 1996 to 410 million Swiss francs, the finance chief of the Geneva-based humanitarian agency said on Wednesday.
Rene Zagolin, who manages the fund for ICRC employees, told Reuters the assets were growing by 40 million francs a year.
Industry estimates say assets under management in public and private pension funds in Switzerland total more than 300 billion Swiss francs and are growing by more than 10 percent a year.
In a sign of the stiff competition in Geneva, Zagolin said the ICRC had been approached by 79 mostly foreign banks alone in 1996 and more than 15 so far this year to manage its funds.
The bulk of ICRC pension fund assets were being managed by two big Geneva-based Swiss private banks and a big Swiss bank, but the agency would start work with U.S. and foreign banks.
"Commissions of foreign banks in Switzerland are lower. They are more dynamic. Swiss banks are expensive," Zagolin said.

The ICRC fund has 365 million Swiss francs in securities and 40 million in real estate. Nearly 40 percent of the portfolio is in shares, a fifth in Swiss equities and the bulk in Europe. The fund has seven percent in cash and the remainder in bonds.

There are some 12,000 pension funds in Switzerland but only a fraction are of interest to banks managing money, industry analysts say. For every pension fund giant like Novartis, with some 100,000 employees, there are dozens of smaller companies.
Aid agencies with pension funds managed out of Switzerland include the Geneva-based world Red Cross body, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies.
